newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW-Japan beauty maker hopes to up dividend.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Japan beauty maker hopes to up dividend.

text.p: Japanese hair care products maker Milbon Co Ltd said it may boost its annual dividend by one to two yen this business year if it meets its earnings estimate.
"We can pay an ordinary dividend of more than 15 yen this business year if the business goes as planned," Milbon president Ichiro Konoike told Reuters in a recent interview.
He said the annual dividend would be raised by one to two yen from the previous year, when it paid an annual dividend of 15 yen per share, including a commemorative dividend of three yen.

Konoike said there would be no change in the firm's annual earnings forecast for the year to December 1997, as it was able to post figures that were in line with its expectations in the first half, he added.

Milbon specialises in goods for professional hair salon use and operates 4,000 beauty parlours in Japan. Konoike said he wants to increase the number of beauty parlours to 5,000 by the end of next year.
Japan's cosmetics market has been booming in recent years as women of all ages and young men have become obsessed with good grooming, especially when it comes to hair care.
In the first half of 1997, Milbon's sales of hair dyeing goods rose by 12 percent year-on-year, while sales of shampoo and related hair care goods rose seven percent, Konoike said.
"Hair dyeing is no longer just a fad but a stable trend. It has become a part of hair styling just as cutting and perming. Demand will keep rising," he said.
Asked about business expansion overseas, Konoike said he sees future possibilities in Asia, but added it will take time for the market there to take off.
The company said it invested 50 million yen during the first half of 1997 to strengthen its manufacturing facilities.
It also spent 1.1 billion yen to build a new beauty parlour in Tokyo, which will be completed in the spring of 1998.
Konoike also said Milbon would be able to achieve its goal of boosting current profit to 10 percent of sales at a date earlier than its initial target of 1999.
"We are working on the new five-year plan. Our new target will be to raise our current profit to 13 percent of our sales," he said.
